slides.heading: Why Verbs Matter?
slides.content: Verbs act as cognitive anchors. They help learners predict meaning, understand relationships, and build mental models of actions and events.
slides.notes: Highlight benefits for visually impaired learners.

slides.heading: How Verbs Support Meaning?
slides.content:
Examples:
• She wears a ___
• He drives a ___
• They cook the ___
Verbs narrow possibilities and improve listening comprehension.
slides.notes: Ask audience to guess the missing nouns.

slides.heading: Verbs Reveal Word Function
slides.content:
Verbs show how nouns participate in actions:
• Something you hold
• Something you visit
• Something you eat
• Something you fix

slides.heading: Cognitive Benefits
slides.content:
Verb-rich instruction improves:
• Semantic networks
• Memory retention
• Contextual guessing
• Top-down listening skills

slides.heading: Shortcomings of Glossaries in Q Skills
slides.content:
Current word lists:
• Focus on nouns and adjectives
• Provide very few or no verb-noun collocations
• Reduce context-based inference

slides.heading: Weak Context Example
slides.content:
Word list:
• apartment
• neighbor
• noise
Without verbs, students struggle to understand relationships.
slides.notes: Show why noun-only lists are insufficient.

slides.heading: Strong Context Example
slides.content:
Add verbs:
• live
• complain
• hear
Learners infer relationships and meaning more easily.

slides.heading: Recommendations / Use Case Scenarios
slides.content:
Enhance Q Skills by:
• Adding high-frequency verbs
• Pairing nouns with collocating verbs
• Including verbs in pre-teaching
• Using verb–noun frames

slides.heading: Teacher Strategies
slides.content:
Teachers can:
• Introduce verbs before nouns
• Use guiding questions
• Create verb-based cloze tasks
• Encourage guessing nouns from actions

slides.heading: Impact on Learners
slides.content:
Verb-focused instruction improves:
• Listening comprehension
• Vocabulary retention
• Contextual guessing
• Confidence and accessibility

slides.heading: Conclusion
slides.content:
• Verbs are essential scaffolds in vocabulary learning
• Q Skills should integrate verbs as a core component of vocabulary instruction.
